title: Materials and Their Meanings
subtitle: Gold, silver, bronze, acacia, linen and scarlet, oil and blood, fire and stone, and the numbers: what the materials of Scripture came to mean
summary: The text never pauses to explain why the altar is bronze and the ark is gold, or why the frames are acacia and the priests wear linen. But Scripture uses its materials with great consistency, sometimes says outright what one means, and the New Testament reads several of them as pictures of Christ and His people. Each entry here gives the anchor passage, then the places that show the pattern and the places that state the meaning. Where a meaning is a long-standing reading rather than a statement of the text, the note says so.

categories.title: Stated in Scripture
categories.note: A passage that gives the meaning outright.

categories.title: Pattern of use
categories.note: The material recurring in the same role, from which the meaning is drawn.

categories.title: Pointing to Christ
categories.note: Where the material becomes a picture of Jesus.

categories.title: The believer and the church
categories.note: Where the material describes God's people.
